newsitem.title: USA: IMF official sees signs of overheating US economy.
newsitem.headline: IMF official sees signs of overheating US economy.

text.p: A senior International Monetary Fund official said Monday he saw some signs that the U.S. economy may be overheating.
"We are holding our breath," the official, who declined to be named, told reporters at a briefing ahead of the start of the IMF/World Bank annual meeting later this week.
At 5.1 percent, the U.S. unemployment rate has fallen beyond the so-called "natural" rate for the economy, he said.
"Possibly one could see some overheating already," he added, pointing in particular to stepped-up wage pressures.
The senior IMF official pegged the long-term sustainable growth rate of the U.S. economy at around 2-1/2 percent.
"One can dream of more," he said, but what the IMF is interested in is sustained growth, not a stop-go pattern.
The senior official declined to say whether he felt the Federal Reserve should raise short-term interest rates on Tuesday to keep inflation in check.
However, IMF First Deputy Managing Director Stanley Fischer told Reuters Financial Television earlier this month that it was "probably about time" for the U.S. central bank to increase rates.
